book.title: Aftermath: The Remnants of War
book.summary: In riveting and revelatory detail, Aftermath documents the ways in which wars have transformed the terrain of the battlefield into landscapes of memory and enduring terror: in France, where millions of acres of farmland are cordoned off to all but a corps of demolition experts responsible for the undetonated bombs and mines of World War I that are now rising up in fields, gardens, and backyards; in a sixty-square-mile area outside Stalingrad that was a cauldron of destruction in 1941 and is today an endless field of bones; in the Nevada deserts, where America waged a hidden nuclear war against itself in the 1950's, the results of which are only now becoming apparent; in Vietnam, where a nation's effort to remove the physical detritus of war has created psychological and genetic devastation; in Kuwait, where terrifyingly sophisticated warfare was followed by the Sisyphean task of making…

evidence: trade publisher signal: Vintage Books / Penguin Random House

argument.statement: Wars transform battlefields into landscapes of memory and enduring terror, leaving physical, psychological, and genetic devastation long after fighting ends.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the enduring impacts of warfare on landscapes and societies, making War & Military the dominant subject, with a secondary focus on History due to its examination of historical contexts.
